thread:
elaine: Heads up — our attestation sweep flagged a provenance + logging gap for the 2026-03 base-image batch. Some images show signed SBOMs but no audit entries in the central audit-log for the cosign keywrap operations.
marco: ugh. do we know which pipeline run(s)?
elaine: quick grep shows registry tags `base-2026-03-{a..f}` from the `bake-ci` pipeline between 02:42-02:55 UTC. audit-log missing for 02:45-02:50 window.
security-bot: ALERT: Missing audit entries detected (cosign:keywrap) — P0 candidate if repros. See /incidents/2026-03-logging-gap for more. :warning:
sam: i'm on it. first thought: likely RBAC change to signer service-account or a KMS rotation glitch. any recent IAM/grant pushes?
anya: runtime didn't touch signing, but we did flip a namespace admission-controller rule yesterday (denyPrivs=false -> true) for canaries. Could that block the bake runner from writing audit events?
marco: that admission change wouldn't stop writes to audit-log service unless the runner lost a role binding to the audit-service account. ops-bot: recent iam diff applied — removed rolebinding `bake-ci->audit-writer` on 2026-03-02 02:43 UTC (change set: iam/changes/523).
elaine: ok that matches window. so RBAC regression removed the audit-writer binding. two questions: 1) can we restore binding and retroactively re-ingest events? 2) do we need to rebuild/resign images to satisfy compliance?
sam: action plan proposal:
- restore rolebinding immediately (marco)
- re-trigger cosign signing step for the affected tags with same key (if key still available) and push audit event
- if key rotated since then -> we MUST re-sign with new envelope and re-run attestation -> partial rebuild might be required if provenance metadata depends on build id
- run vuln-scan patch on any images that land in the rebuild window (glibc CVE noted on 02-28)
marco: i'll restore binding now.
marco: done — recreated rolebinding bake-ci -> audit-writer. verifying event acceptance...
security-bot: IAM binding restored by marco at 02:58 UTC.
sam: trying a dry-run re-sign:```sh
# dry-run re-sign to emit audit event without changing image digest
cosign sign --key k8s://secret/cosign/bake-ci --annotations build_id=2026-03-02-0245 --dryrun base.registry.io/base-2026-03-a
```
sam: dry-run successful locally; audit service emitted a "cosign:sign:attempt" event but marked source=dryrun. Need an actual sign to get full attestation.
anya: runtime policy — if we re-sign the same image digest with same key, do downstream caches invalidate? i.e., will KV caches or shard placements confuse runtime?
marco: re-signing doesn't change image digest; cosign attaches external signatures. runtime caches keyed on image digest + manifest, so should be safe. we just need to ensure manifest references don't change.
jamie: compliance question — does adding a signature later satisfy the regulatory window? our SOC auditor expects continuous audit trail at time-of-sign. retroactive signatures are tricky.
elaine: good point. Ops/legal: can we produce a forensics packet showing the sign timestamp, the rolebinding change, and the remediation steps? jamie: yes, we can compile a packet but we should treat this as a partial breach of process and do a canary rebuild if sign key rotated or if vuln patches applied.
marco: status update: the key used by bake-ci is still present in KMS (no rotations recorded since Feb). so we can re-sign without rekeying.
sam: i'll run a targeted re-sign for tags a..f and push. command:```sh
for t in a b c d e f; do
  cosign sign --key k8s://secret/cosign/bake-ci base.registry.io/base-2026-03-$t && echo "signed $t" || echo "fail $t"
done
```
sam: started. logging goes to /var/logs/audit-proxy and should show cosign events. will attach event IDs to PR.
elaine: while that's running, can eng-runtime validate that signatures are discoverable by adopters (attestation lookup)? any chance runtime blocks signature discovery for rootless pods?
anya: i'll run quick checks against canary clusters and the attestation cache. if not discoverable, we may need to bump an indexer.
ops-bot: vulnerability scanner found 3 images in the affected tag set with medium CVE (glibc) — tickets created #VLN-1223 #VLN-1224 #VLN-1225.
marco: if re-sign succeeds and audit events ingest, we'll mark this P1->P2 and close incident. if any re-sign fails because KMS denies access, escalate to KMS oncall.
sam: all six signed successfully; audit entries visible: event_ids [evt-9812, evt-9813, evt-9814, evt-9815, evt-9816, evt-9817]. pushed a short runbook: https://wiki.redwood/infrasec/attestation-reingest-2026-03.
jamie: thanks. legal wants the forensics packet and a note about why this happened (human IAM change). pls include timeline and who approved the rolebinding removal.
marco: recorded timeline in the runbook + linked iam change set (iam/changes/523) and PR that removed binding.
elaine: next steps (assignments):
- sam: attach audit event IDs and runbook to incident ticket and ping compliance (done)
- marco: coordinate a short pod-canary to validate signature discovery across regions (ongoing)
- anya: validate runtime attestation lookup and indexer (by EOD)
- security: write a blameless postmortem and propose an IAM guardrail (prevent rolebinding deletions without approval)
- ops: schedule patch rebuilds for VLN-1223..1225 if tests fail on canary
marco: also proposing an automated CI check that fails pipeline if `audit-writer` rolebinding is absent for any signer SA. I'll prototype.
elaine: thanks all. closing loop — if anything fails escalate to @oncall-kms and post in #incidents. :thumbsup:
